title: rubus chaerophyllus subsp. axillaris
intro: Rubus chaerophyllus subsp. axillaris, commonly known as wild raspberry or Alpine raspberry, is a subspecies of shrub in the rose family. It is native to the mountainous regions of Europe and Asia, and its leaves, stems, and roots have been traditionally used for their medicinal properties, including its potential to treat various health issues such as gastrointestinal problems, fever, and inflammation. The plant is reported to have therapeutic actions including anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant effects, which may contribute to its potential health benefits, including reducing oxidative stress and improving cardiovascular health. The bioactive constituents of Rubus chaerophyllus subsp. axillaris include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and tannins, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
